title: IdP integration consumer contracts and validation catalog
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a single-source "consumer contract" and validation catalog that defines the exact SAML/OIDC assertions, claim shapes, timing expectations, and failure modes Redwood services (authn/authz/audit) will accept from each supported IdP (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Ping). Goal: reduce flaky customer integrations by 50% and provide deterministic validator tooling used in onboarding and regression tests.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable contract exists for each IdP that enumerates required/optional attributes, allowed NameID formats, audience/issuer checks, sign/alg constraints, and recommended attribute fallback rules
A validation utility (CLI) implements these contracts and returns structured error codes we can map to user-facing troubleshooting guidance
A test catalog with representative sample assertions for each Okta/Azure/Google/Ping variant (including known vendor quirks) is checked into the repo and runnable in CI
RBAC v2 role-mapping examples per IdP documented and validated against the audit logger so every assignment emits the expected audit event
Playbook snippets for resolver behavior on missing group claims and clock skew are in Confluence and linked from onboarding flow
steps: Survey existing customer incidents and extract recurring attribute/NameID failure patterns (owner: Owen)
Draft consumer contracts for Okta/Azure/Google/Ping with fields: required_attributes, optional_attributes, nameid_formats, saml_clock_skew_sla, audience_regex, signature_algorithms
Implement Validator CLI that ingests a SAML assertion or OIDC id_token and returns pass/fail plus standardized error codes
Create sample assertion corpus (valid + 6 classes of invalid) and add to integration-tests repository
Wire validator into onboarding pipeline: preflight checks during Private deployment bootstrap and console-guided connector tests
Run full CI matrix across supported connector versions and add as required check for admin docs PRs
comments: 2025-03-02 - Owen Brooks: Kickoff notes uploaded; initial incident digest shows 38% of SSO failures caused by malformed group claims or missing audience. Prioritize audience/nameid checks.
2025-03-06 - Asha Patel: Draft contract schema v0.1 posted to Confluence. Using 'attribute-set' approach (email, uid, groups, roles, sessionNotOnOrAfter). Added example mappings to RBAC v2 roles.

2025-03-10 - Security review (prelim): J. Moreno flagged that SHA1 signatures still seen in older Ping instances; validator must return a warning code but allow override only for Dedicated/Private with explicit admin opt-in.

2025-03-12 - Marco Diaz (QA): Added 12 sample assertions (Okta: group-in-claim vs groups-in-attribute; Azure: roles_in_token; Google: nameid_format variations). Found Azure emits 'ipaddr' audience in some tenant setups; added audience_regex to contract.

2025-03-15 - PR 18 merged: Validator returns standardized error codes (IDP_AUD_MISMATCH, IDP_SIG_WEAK, IDP_MISSING_GROUPS, IDP_CLOCK_SKEW) and a machine-readable JSON output for the console. Next: integrate output -> user-facing troubleshooting doc.

2025-03-18 - Owen Brooks: Running CI matrix. Two failing cases remain: legacy Ping instances with SHA1 and Okta orgs sending groups as comma-separated string in single attribute. Plan: add migration note + automated parser for comma-list groups behind feature flag.
